note: Entry based on the original description of Desneux 1904 (soldier, alate); the source text is a library OCR of the BHL fascicle.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Total length about 3.4 mm; head length (including the nasus) about 1.5 mm. Head reddish brown, the nasus slightly darker, more or less pear-shaped; the posterior part inflated and rounded; the base of the nasus with a swelling whose sides are almost parallel. Nasus elongate and slender. In lateral view the nasus and the anterior swelling of the head lie in a straight line, forming a distinct angle with the posterior part of the head. Antennae long, 13 segments, segment 3 at least twice as long as segment 2. Pronotum saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe raised vertically with an entire margin, the posterior lobe strongly narrowed. Legs elongate.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body length about 4 mm. Head reddish brown, round, strongly convex dorsally. Antennae 14 segments, segment 3 slightly less than twice as long as segment 2. Thorax of the same shape as in the soldier. Abdomen inflated; the tergites slightly tinged with brown.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Originally published as Termes tenuirostris n. sp. Localities: Jalisco state, Mexico (collected by Diguet 1900, the label recording 'nesting on a tree'); also Orizaba (collected by Bilimek, Vienna museum). The original emphasized that the soldier head shape is characteristic of the species.
